memo.headline: Low Coverage for Regular Fit Kurta Requires Immediate Chart Adjustment

sections.heading: Current Chart Coverage
sections.body: The current garment size chart for the regular fit kurta covers 27.1% of the population. A large portion of the market is missed, with no size recommended for 51.5% of the population, and 72.9% of the population finding no good size. When a fit works, the best size distribution is 6.9% for S, 12.4% for M, 16.4% for L, and 12.9% for XL.

sections.heading: Where the Chart Loses Buyers
sections.body: The chart loses many buyers because the garment is tight at the hip and short in the sleeve length. The hip is tight for 75.9% of size S buyers, 61.0% of size M buyers, and 43.0% of size L buyers. The sleeve length is short for 72.6% of size S buyers, 63.2% of size M buyers, 62.9% of size L buyers, and 64.0% of size XL buyers. Additionally, the shoulder width is loose for 37.7% of size L buyers.

sections.heading: Recommended Grading Adjustments
sections.body: We can increase coverage from 27.1% to 36.5% by adjusting specific garment measurements. For the shoulder width, adjust size S from 42.5 cm to 40.5 cm (a change of -2.0 cm) to gain 3.0% coverage alone. Adjust size M shoulder width from 44.0 cm to 43.0 cm (a change of -1.0 cm) to gain 1.2%, and adjust size XL shoulder width from 47.0 cm to 48.0 cm (a change of 1.0 cm) to gain 1.3%. For the chest, adjust size S from 104.0 cm to 106.0 cm (a change of 2.0 cm) to gain 0.7%, adjust size M from 110.0 cm to 112.0 cm (a change of 2.0 cm) to gain 0.5%, and adjust size XL from 122.0 cm to 120.0 cm (a change of -2.0 cm) to gain 0.2%.

sections.heading: Caveat
sections.body: Synthetic population from a statistical stand-in with invented body-measurement distributions, not the SMPL shape space. Calibrate with consented, anonymized twins before relying on it.
